cs.t: Between my father and I we have 11 Nikon DSLRs starting from 2005.  I think 8 of them were made in Thailand and 3 were made in Japan.  They all work fine.  One of the Thailand cameras had a shutter issue after 2 years and I had it repaired.  All of the other cameras have been flawless.  Even my D70 from 2005 was made in Thailand and still works today although I converted it to infrared use.
I would be willing to bet I have photos in my archive that cannot be reproduced on any modern smartphone, that I took in ~2004 with a Nikon D70.
cs.th: iPhone 16 cameras vs. traditional digital cameras

cs.t: You don't need very big pockets for that. Today you can find very affordable monochromatic astrophotography cameras, and you can also modify cheap DSLR cameras or even compact cameras to remove its IR/UV/low pass filters. You can even insert a different semi permanent internal filter after that (like a IR or UV band pass) I've done a Nikon D70 DSLR and a Canon Ixus/Elph compact. Some cameras are very easy, some very difficult, so better check first some tutorials before buying a camera. And there are companies doing the conversion for you for a bunch of hundred dollars (probably 300 or 400).
